findings.claim: The inspected retail PE has no COFF symbols/file records, debug directory payload or recognized CodeView/PDB signature, and no useful original source-file identifier was recovered in the documented PE/history search.
findings.limitations: Limited inspection scope; incidental MAP resource names and library/compiler metadata are not source provenance. No claim about private, unreachable or untracked artifacts.

findings.claim: Nine provisional TU fragments group 41 of 42 bounded defined functions, with forwarding thunk 00493150 unassigned; no original filenames or independently verified compilation units were recovered.
findings.limitations: Schema medium corresponds to MODERATE. Confidence concerns candidate coupling; fragments may merge or subdivide. Functional responsibility, direct calls and state access do not establish original C file linkage.

findings.claim: The map-to-loader and texture-wrapper-to-PIX transitions offer the strongest tested separation hypotheses, while the mission preparation-to-tactics cut remains LOW and no boundary reaches HIGH.
findings.limitations: No source ground truth or object-contribution records. Ordinary alignment, switch tables, interleaved thunks, shared configuration and larger single-file alternatives limit discrimination.

findings.claim: Deterministic extraction and exact original-byte checks establish the reviewed static facts but do not justify an authoritative whole-executable TU partition.
findings.limitations: 100 factual checks and manual relationship reviews do not calibrate source-file inference accuracy. Exploratory ranking is potentially useful; full executable partitioning remains unjustified.
